  Readable gloss: "Hagar (hagar, possibly 'flight' or 'stranger') is the Egyptian maidservant of Sarah whom Abraham took as a concubine at Sarah's suggestion when Sarah remained childless (Gen 16:1-3). After conceiving Ishmael, Hagar was driven out by Sarah's harsh treatment and fled into the wilderness, where the angel of the Lord found her by a spring on the road to Shur and promised her innumerable descendants (Gen 16:7-14). She became the only person in Genesis to give God a name: El Roi, 'the God who sees me.' Later, after Isaac's birth, she and Ishmael were expelled permanently, and God again preserved them in the wilderness of Beersheba (Gen 21:9-21). Paul allegorizes Hagar as representing the covenant of Sinai and slavery in Galatians 4:24-25. Spanish, French, and German all retain the name Hagar (French: Agar)."
